purpose: Use actual external professional SyGuS synthesizer, NOT another hand-coded bounded enumerator, to assess if first G1 neural claims are simply weaker than standard specialist.
external_originals: FROZEN eight SyGuS-Org/benchmarks comp/2018/PBE_Strings_Track from existing G1 external prereg, no task additions or deletions
assessor: apt installed cvc5 CLI, exact version printed, published original SyGuS grammar and original inputs except *LAST* constraint; last constraint gold never passed to synthesizer, only independent postfreeze validation.
variants: Try --lang=sygus2 --sygus then --lang=sygus1 --sygus ONLY as dialect compatibility, never different source task split, solver, grammar or original gold.
failure_policy: Solver error, unsupported syntax, timeout, no parseable solution, invalid training semantics, untrusted full grammar, no ground SMT verifier => UNSUPPORTED/UNKNOWN, not successful specialist proof. No claim of equivalence for arbitrary strings from finite PBE examples.
safe_validation: Fresh cvc5 SMT-LIB ground equality for each original TRAIN and withheld LAST constraint after candidate program frozen; syntactically reported synthesis not a pass until validation.
fixed_non_leakage: Remove only final original (constraint...) form from full source, preserve unchanged grammar; parse exact original constraints and source identifier before deleting, hash both train-only and original source.
interpretation: If cvc5 solves original where student fails, demonstrates missing coverage and strong-classical precedence; if both fail, result insufficient for learning advantage. Never claim student > specialist from a single timeout.
matched_cost_limit: Published original grammar is much more expressive than student 225. This is deliberately stronger-rights expert reference, not equal-rights efficiency comparison. Any CPU timing from apt cvc5 and numpy first in different runner cannot support 10x claim.
